name: Ahmedabad
title: Ahmedabad: who is doing what about heat?
scope: Organisations and activities identified in public sources, read on 28 November 2026. It is not a complete list of everyone working on heat in Ahmedabad, and no organisation was contacted.

orientation.text: Ahmedabad wrote South Asia's first city heat action plan in 2013, after the 2010 heat wave, and an evaluation cited by the WHO Foundation credits it with lives saved. Since then the work has spread from warnings to homes, streets and income: cool roofs, a misted bus stop and a heat insurance for women in informal work, much of it carried by one women's housing organisation working with the city.

unknowns: How many roofs the initiative has coated since 2019, when NRDC gave a figure of over 100.
How many women hold the heat insurance, and the total paid out.
orgs.outside: It works on heat plans in other cities (Churu and Varanasi, among others); that work is not counted here.
orgs.name: Mahila Housing Trust
orgs.summary: A women's housing organisation that runs the Cool Roofs Initiative in the city's heat plan, a misted bus stop with the city, and a heat insurance for women in informal work.

unknowns: Its current role in the city's plan.
orgs.outside: Its cool roof work in Telangana and elsewhere is counted on those cities' profiles.
orgs.name: Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC), India programme
orgs.summary: A partner of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation on the 2017 cool roof pilot and the city-wide programme that followed.

unknowns: Its current role in the plan and in evaluating it was not read for this profile.
orgs.name: Indian Institute of Public Health Gandhinagar
orgs.summary: A partner of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation on the 2017 cool roof pilot.

authorities.name: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation
authorities.role: Leads the Heat Action Plan, first launched in 2013, and the city's cool roof programme.

outputs: Parks open from 6 am to 11 pm for shade (as reported in March 2025)
activities.evaluation: An evaluation by researchers credits the plan with 1,190 lives saved a year in its first five years; the evaluation itself was not read for this profile.
activities.title: Heat Action Plan with early warnings
activities.desc: The city's plan, first launched in 2013: an early warning system, awareness campaigns, and since 2017 cool roofs. Scroll reported that parks stay open for shade, signboards explain heatstroke and all departments meet weekly on the plan.

activities.evaluation: Not evaluated in the sources read.
activities.title: Cool roof pilot on 3,000 low-income homes (2017)
activities.desc: Roofs of over 3,000 low-income homes painted with white lime paint under the Heat Action Plan, by city staff, student volunteers and civil society groups. In 2018 real estate developers were asked to apply cool roofs to private buildings voluntarily.

collaborators: included cool roofs in the Heat Action Plan
outputs: Roofs coated (number not stated in the 2025 sources)
activities.evaluation: Not evaluated in the sources read.
activities.title: Cool Roofs Initiative in low-income homes
activities.desc: Heat-reflective paint on the roofs of low-income homes, run by Mahila Housing Trust within the city's Heat Action Plan. In 2019 the city was preparing a city-wide programme; by 2025 the city had included cool roofs in its plan.

outputs: One bus stop fitted with misting
activities.evaluation: Mahila Housing Trust reports at least 4 to 7°C of relief; no independent measurement was found.
activities.title: Misted cool bus stop at Lal Darwaza
activities.desc: A high-pressure misting system at one bus stop, installed by Mahila Housing Trust with the city.

activities.evaluation: Not evaluated in the sources read.

equity.receiving: Women in informal work who hold the insurance.

activities.title: Heat insurance for women in informal work
activities.desc: A parametric insurance that pays women a fixed sum when temperatures cross set thresholds, so a lost day's earnings is partly covered without a claim. Launched in April 2024; a payout was triggered in May 2024.

money.what: Total cost of the 2017 cool roof pilot
money.stage_note: Given by NRDC as the programme's total cost for 2017.

timeline.text: A heat wave; experts later estimated heat contributed to more than 1,000 deaths.
The Heat Action Plan is launched, the first by a city in South Asia.
Cool roof pilot on over 3,000 low-income homes.
A city-wide cool roof programme in draft.
Heat insurance for women in informal work launched.
A temperature threshold is crossed and insurance payouts follow.

gaps: How many roofs have been coated city-wide since the 2017 pilot, and how many were maintained.
The current edition of the Heat Action Plan was not read for this profile; its partners and budget are not described here.
Whether the cool roofs, the misted bus stop or the insurance have been independently evaluated.
Gujarati-language sources were not searched systematically for this first version.

contradictions.text: Heat insurance terms: Down To Earth (June 2025) describes two thresholds of 43.7°C and 44.1°C, paying Rs 750 and a further Rs 1,250; the WHO Foundation (September 2024) describes one trigger of 44.2 ºC and Rs 2,000 a season. They may describe different seasons of the scheme.

start_here.text: The 2017 pilot shows what a first cool roof season involved: who painted, with what, at what stated cost.
The heat insurance is a working example of paying for a lost day of work without a claim form.

method_note: Sources were found by web search in English; local-language sources were not searched systematically. Where a source could not be read, nothing rests on it.
